chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn 'Utba said:

I asked him about a man for whom I designate a sum of money, or for whom there is a debt due to me prior to that, and he asks me for money which I increase upon the money I already have due from him. Is it permissible that I increase him money and sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, so I say to him: 'I sell you this pearl for one thousand dirhams on the condition that I defer you by its price and by the money I have due from you for such and such months?' He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell an item on credit at a higher price while deferring payment of an existing debt?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith illustrates the permissibility of *bay' al-mu'ajjal* (deferred sale) as a mechanism for debt restructuring, where the seller inflates the price to cover the deferred principal. This practice, often linked to *tawarruq*, allows creditors to effectively extend credit without explicit interest, reflecting the pragmatic flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in commercial transactions. The Imam’s simple affirmation ('La ba'sa') underscores the validity of this common financial arrangement in early Islamic markets.
